qualitative.gate_2_reason: Approximately 40-50% of underlying group earnings are generated in Latin America and emerging markets (principally Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Argentina), exposing capital to severe currency depreciation, political volatility, and emerging-market credit cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (emerging-market earnings concentration, REJECT). Banco Santander derives roughly 40-50% of its net profit from Latin American emerging markets (principally Brazil, Mexico, Chile, and Argentina). This structural exposure subjects euro-based compounding to ongoing currency debasement, heightened sovereign/political risk, and volatile credit cycles.
qualitative.evidence: Globally diversified retail and commercial banking giant. Attributable net profit in 2023 of €11.1B and 2024 of €12.6B heavily reliant on South America and Mexico (~40-50% of underlying earnings). Brazil alone has historically contributed 20-30% of group profit. Returns in euro terms are continually eroded by Latin American currency devaluation (BRL, ARS) and credit risk provisions.
